meta.title: Alex Writes to Tom
meta.textType: functional: an email and a reply (two texts to compare)

paragraphs: On Thursday, April twenty-second, Tom opened an email from his pen pal Alex. Lily stood behind him, and Pip lay under the desk with a yellow sponge. The screen showed two photos, a boy on a surfboard and a small gray robot. "Dear Tom, I hope that you and Pip are well." "This week, I had a big adventure with my cousin." "He has a surfboard, and he showed me how to use it." "First, I fell off the surfboard six times." "Then I stood up for five seconds." "Finally, I rode a small wave, and my cousin took the photo." "I am also a big fan of robots." "One day, I want to invent a robot that washes cars." "My robot needs a bigger battery, so I saved twenty dollars." "A boy in the robot chatroom likes this battery, and he says that it is the best." "The software for my robot is easy to download, and I love technology." "How is Pip?" "Best wishes, Alex."

Tom wrote his reply, and he added a photo of Pip. "Dear Alex, thank you for your email and your photos." "I do not surf, but I fall off my bike a lot." "I want to buy football boots, so I wash bikes in our garden for thirty baht a bike." "First, I saved one hundred and eighty baht." "Then I found an advertisement for the boots that I want." "Finally, I will buy them when I have eight hundred baht." "I hope that you invent a robot that washes bikes!" "This photo shows Pip with the yellow sponge." "Best wishes, Tom."

Lily read the two letters again. "What is the same in your two letters?" she asked. Tom looked at the screen and said, "I do not know." Lily took her notebook and drew a table with two columns. She wrote "Alex" and "Tom" at the top. Down the side, she wrote three questions: where, what first, and money for.

"Where?" asked Lily. "Alex writes about the sea, and I write about our garden," said Tom. "What first?" asked Lily. "Alex fell off the surfboard first, and I saved baht first," said Tom. "Money for?" asked Lily. "Alex saves dollars for a battery, and I save baht for boots," said Tom. Lily wrote every answer in the table.

Lily put down her pencil and looked at the table. "You both save money for something new," she said. "You both write about Pip at the end, too." "The big difference is the place." "Alex has an adventure at the sea, but you have one in the garden." Tom laughed. "My adventure is wet, too," he said.
Tom read his reply once more. "Send it," said Lily. Tom pressed the button on the screen. Under the desk, Pip held the yellow sponge and did not move.
text.summary: Tom reads an email from his pen pal Alex about surfing and a robot, and he writes a reply about washing bikes for football boots. Lily draws a table to compare the two letters.
